solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: China last to claim victory, symbolically

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so china is a pal

indicators.note: 'last to' points at the final letter of the following word, claim

explanation.surface: A boast that China is finally about to claim a symbolic victory.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA is Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate.
explanation.definitionFit: The frond of the palm tree was carried as an emblem of triumph, hence 'bear the palm' for winning.

clue.text: A religious sect north of river, devoted to queen and her workers?

definitions.text: devoted to queen and her workers?

indicators.note: in a down clue 'north of' puts the earlier pieces above the river

parts.note: pi is slang short for pious, religious
a cult is a religious sect
the Ural is a river in Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A devout sect up north of a river worships its queen and her workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen and workers are bees, not a monarch and staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiculture is beekeeping, devoted to the queen bee and her worker bees.

clue.text: Victoria's first PM providing her capital?

definitions.meaning: Lord ... was Queen Victoria's first prime minister
the city is the capital of the Australian state of Victoria

explanation.surface: A question whether the young Queen's first Prime Minister also supplied her capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her' switches from the queen to the Australian state of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to the Whig premier Viscount Melbourne and the state capital of Victoria.

clue.text: Ordering audit from time to time, no women being involved?

indicators.note: 'being involved' says one group of letters is wrapped up inside the other
taking letters only now and then means every other letter of the word audit

parts.note: a company with no women in it is just men

explanation.surface: A firm's books are put in order by occasional audits run with no women taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordering' is the noun sense of putting in order; 'being involved' tucks the men inside the letters 'from time to time' picks out.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjustment is a setting in order or putting right, so ordering serves as its synonym.

clue.text: Many uncovered poet quite slowly

indicators.note: uncovered means with the outer letters stripped off, leaving the middle of many

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: Many poets, once exposed, turn out to be rather slow.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning at a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: What disillusioned preacher may do for lords and ladies?

definitions.meaning: to jack something in is to quit it, so a preacher who has lost faith may quit the pulpit
a British name for the wild arum plant, cuckoo-pint

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what a disenchanted minister might do for the nobility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lords and ladies' is not the gentry but a woodland plant; the answer is the name of a related arum.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a plant name for a hooded arum and, read literally, quitting the preacher's stand.

clue.text: America must cut pollution to keep up

indicators.note: 'must cut' means the word for America slices into the word for pollution

parts.note: a stain is a contamination or blemish
US stands for the United States of America

explanation.surface: An environmental plea: America must reduce pollution to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to maintain it or keep it going.

clue.text: Lifts, commonly for high part of building

indicators.note: 'commonly' signals casual speech that drops the aitch at the start of words

parts.note: to heave is to lift something heavy

explanation.surface: Lifts, as they are usually called, serve the upper part of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' imitates Cockney speech, where the H is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: The overhanging lower edge of a roof sits high on a building.

clue.text: Dilatory sailor on duty cleared out

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: with its inside emptied, only the outside letters of duty remain

explanation.surface: A slow sailor, when on duty, gets thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone slow or late in doing what is expected.

clue.text: Dinosaur's decline complete in the vicinity

parts.note: a dip is a fall or decline

indicators.note: 'in' places the word for complete inside the word for the vicinity

parts.note: a locus is a place or area, the spot where something is
to do a job is to complete it

explanation.surface: A dinosaur's decline is total in the surrounding region.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Dinosaur's' stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The diplodocus is a very long-necked plant-eating sauropod of the Jurassic period.

clue.text: Heading to the back, wander past

indicators.note: the heading, or first letter, of the word for wander travels to the end

parts.note: to rove is to wander

explanation.surface: An instruction to walk on past, heading to the back of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Over can mean finished or gone by, as in 'the summer is over', the sense of past.

clue.text: Old sailors on ship prompt to turn criminal

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the old sailors follow the ship

parts.note: sub is short for submarine, a vessel
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: Veteran sailors aboard a vessel encourage mutiny or some other crime.
explanation.definitionFit: To suborn is to induce someone, by bribery or persuasion, to commit a crime such as perjury.

clue.text: Wild daisy covering most of area, maybe

indicators.note: 'covering' means the scrambled flower letters wrap around the other piece
wild means out of control, so the letters of daisy are scattered
'most of' drops the final letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Wild daisies have spread over most of the area, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' is the anagram signal and 'covering' wraps its result around the shortened area; 'maybe' is the definition, a hedging phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a conversational hedge meaning probably or perhaps, much like maybe.

clue.text: Freak may be on trial abroad, after English withdrawal

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oddity might be put on trial overseas after an Englishman pulls out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after English withdrawal' takes one E from MAY BE ON TRIAL before 'abroad' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A freak is an anomaly or something out of the normal run.

clue.text: Jump, ultimately failing to take the lead

indicators.note: 'ultimately' points to the last letter, and 'failing' says that letter goes missing

parts.note: to start is to jump in surprise

explanation.surface: A competitor's jump eventually fails, costing the chance to go in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To star is to play the leading role, as in a film or show.

clue.text: Snarling Parisian in stern of boat, Walton's craft

parts.note: French for 'in' is en

indicators.note: the stern is the rear of a vessel, so this takes the last letter of boat

parts.note: Izaak Walton wrote The Compleat Angler, so his craft is fishing with rod and line

explanation.surface: A snarling Frenchman sits at the back of a boat, practising fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Izaak Walton was the 17th-century English author of The Compleat Angler.
explanation.definitionFit: Snarling as in tangling, the way a fishing line snarls or knots up.

clue.text: Alternative to "ridiculous" one's put out

indicators.note: an alternative version of the word means its letters rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone offering a near-synonym for the word ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's put out' removes an I from RIDICULOUS before rearranging; the whole clue also defines the result as a substitute word.
explanation.definitionFit: The two words are near-synonyms, both meaning absurd or laughable.

clue.text: Impious bishop on island about to engage in affair

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' puts the bishop after the island

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

indicators.note: 'to engage in' sends the word for about inside the word for affair

parts.note: an event is an occasion or affair
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A churchman stuck on an island gets drawn into an affair, which is hardly pious.
explanation.walkthrough: Right Reverend is the formal style of an Anglican bishop; 'to engage in' splits the affair word after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone irreverent shows no respect for sacred things, which is what impious means.

clue.text: Second person with false bottom in English town

indicators.note: in a down clue 'bottom' places the word for false underneath

parts.note: in Genesis Eve was created after Adam, the second human
sham means fake or false

explanation.surface: Another person, a phoney at bottom, turns up in an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Evesham is a market town in Worcestershire. 'Second person' looks like grammar ('you') but is Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Evesham is a market town in Worcestershire, England.

clue.text: Plastic denture kept for an agreed time

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters can be reshaped

explanation.surface: A plastic denture held on to for a set period.
explanation.definitionFit: A post held with tenure is kept securely for a contracted period.

clue.text: Stitch-up that's annoyed me

definitions.meaning: to mend a hole by sewing across it is to repair it with stitches
a mild exclamation of irritation, a polite form of 'damn'

explanation.surface: A grumble about being framed or cheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitch-up' looks like the British slang for a frame-up, but here it is plain sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is repairing a sock by sewing; the other is a mild oath used when irritated.

clue.text: Brand one lover "short of ecstasy", taking another

indicators.note: 'short of' means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: an old flame is a former lover
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
another lover, a beau is a boyfriend

explanation.surface: A tale of one lover, down on drugs, who takes up with somebody else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand' is a burning stick or torch, not a trademark.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, and a brand is an old word for a piece of burning wood.

clue.text: Initial "R" in one's own writing

indicators.note: 'in' places the letter inside the word for handwriting

parts.note: fist is an informal word for handwriting

explanation.surface: An initial R written in one's own hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initial' looks as if it describes the R but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: First and initial both mean coming at the start.

clue.text: I'm surprised to secure record top mark

indicators.note: 'to secure' means the exclamation holds the other piece inside

parts.note: aha is an exclamation of surprise
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A delighted reaction at getting a record top grade.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpha is the highest grade in British marking schemes, from the first Greek letter.

clue.text: Bees take it from flowers close by, bordering court

indicators.note: 'bordering' says the word for close by forms the edges around the other piece

parts.note: near means close by

explanation.surface: Bees gather from blooms nearby, on the edge of a courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: This sugary liquid is what bees collect from blossoms to make honey.

clue.text: Reportedly keeps back vital equipment for tower

indicators.note: 'back' says the held letters are read in the opposite direction
'keeps' means the first word holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: Rumour has it some vital kit for a tower is being held back.
explanation.walkthrough: A tower here is one who tows, though a bell-ringer in a church tower needs one too.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that tows needs a strong cord or line to pull with.

clue.text: Like some curves, deliberately exaggerated

definitions.meaning: the hyperbola is one of the conic sections, so a curve can be of that shape

explanation.surface: A description of curves drawn larger than life.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is geometry, relating to a hyperbola; the other is rhetoric, given to overstatement.

clue.text: Converted coaches, not one fitted with silencer?

indicators.note: 'not' says the following item is taken away

parts.note: to coach is to train
I is the Roman numeral for one
a muted instrument or gun has a silencer on

explanation.surface: A conversion of coaches, all but one given silencers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coaches' looks like vehicles, but is the verb train.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmute something is to change it into another form, as alchemists hoped to turn lead to gold.

clue.text: Veggie food seaman from East always rejected

indicators.note: reading from the east, right to left in an across clue, turns the letters round

parts.note: OS stands for ordinary seaman

indicators.note: 'rejected' means thrown back, so these letters are reversed

parts.note: ay is an old word for ever or always

explanation.surface: A sailor from the East who always turns down vegetarian food.
explanation.definitionFit: The soya bean is a staple protein in vegetarian cooking, as in tofu and soy milk.
